# Matching evaluation (synthetic)

Offline harness for the deterministic matching pipeline.

**The dataset is synthetic.** `data/synthetic_pairs.json` was generated by
`generate_dataset.py` (fixed seed) and contains invented reports. Coordinates are
the public campus place points from `app/geo/uet_lahore.json`. The numbers below
describe this dataset only. They are not measured accuracy on real lost-and-found
reports.

## Dataset

- 50 lost queries across 10 item types (backpack, wallet, phone, keys, bottle, laptop,
  watch, earbuds, ID card, jacket).
- 50 true pairs. The found report shares the item type and usually the colour and
  place. Descriptions are paraphrased from templates, and some fields are omitted on
  either side.
- 250 hard negatives, five per query, built to look like the query's item:
  `hn-lookalike` (same type, colour and brand, found days later elsewhere),
  `hn-brand` (different brand), `hn-colour` (different colour), `hn-before-loss`
  (found before the loss), `hn-category` (same colour, different item type).
- 30 unrelated found reports.
- Every lost query is scored against all 330 found reports. Retrieval, scoring and
  notification selection are the production code paths.

## Metrics

| Metric | Definition |
|---|---|
| precision@1 | Of the queries that have a true match, the share whose top-ranked candidate is that match. Ranking only, no threshold. |
| recall@threshold | True pairs that would be notified (score ≥ threshold and within `max_candidates`) ÷ true pairs. |
| recall (retrieved) | True pairs that survive candidate retrieval at any score ÷ true pairs. |
| FPR (all negatives) | Notified non-matching pairs ÷ all non-matching pairs (lost × found − true). |
| FPR (hard negatives) | Notified hard negatives built for the same query ÷ hard negatives. |
| precision of notifications | True notified ÷ all notified. |
| notifications per query | Notified pairs ÷ queries. Measures notification load. |

## Run

```powershell
cd backend
.\.venv\Scripts\python -m evaluation.generate_dataset   # only if the generator changes
.\.venv\Scripts\python -m evaluation.run_eval --label baseline
```

Results are written to `results/<label>.json`, including per-type false-positive
counts and the top false-positive examples with their explanations.

## Limitations

- Templated text is easier than real descriptions. Recall here is likely optimistic.
- No Roman-Urdu or misspelled descriptions are included.
- Only lost-side queries are evaluated. Found-side queries are not measured.
- Hard negatives are constructed by rules. They do not represent the full range of real look-alikes.
